label: Home Assistant
description: Lights, shutters, sensors, scenes — your home automation setup
agentGuide: Two ways in, same service_id. (1) The REST API, through call_external_service, paths under /api/. GET /api/states lists EVERY entity with its state — the way to discover what exists here, no documentation can tell you; GET /api/states/<entity_id> for one. To act on a device: POST /api/services/<domain>/<service> with a JSON body {"entity_id": "light.living_room"} — light/turn_on, switch/toggle, climate/set_temperature, scene/turn_on; GET /api/services lists the services. POST /api/template renders a template. POST /api/config/automation/config/<id> (script and scene alike) creates or replaces one, on a card. (2) The WebSocket API, through ha_command and ha_listen — what administers the installation: the registries (config/entity_registry/list, …/update with new_entity_id, name, area_id; devices, areas, floors, labels), the dashboards (lovelace/…), the config entries and their flows, ZHA and Z-Wave JS, and the events as they happen (ha_listen, to see a new device arrive). A read runs at once; a change shows the user a card. Entity ids have the form <domain>.<name> and differ from one installation to another: never invent them, read them.
